heroHeadline: Federal Judge Upholds Trump Mail-In Voting Order; DOJ Opens Criminal Probe into E. Jean Carroll; Iran Ceasefire Under Maximum Strain as Kuwait Intercepts Ballistic Missile — Day 494
heroSubtitle: On May 28, 2026 (Day 494 of Trump's second term, Day 89 of the US-Iran war), the Justice Department under Acting AG Todd Blanche opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll for alleged perjury in her civil suit testimony against Trump — Carroll won approximately $88M in damages across two civil trials. The Iran ceasefire came under maximum strain: Kuwait intercepted a ballistic missile (CENTCOM: 'an egregious ceasefire violation'), Iran's IRGC claimed a strike on a US air base in the Persian Gulf (retaliation for US self-defense strikes near Bandar Abbas Airport, May 25-26), and Trump threatened Oman — previously a neutral diplomatic mediator — over an Oman-Iran plan for Strait of Hormuz transit tolls, saying Oman would 'behave or we'll have to blow them up.' Trump declared his annual physical results 'PERFECTLY' healthy. CNN also reported Republicans finished the 2026 redistricting cycle approximately 10 seats ahead of Democrats — a structural advantage that may prevent Democrats from retaking the House even amid Trump's approval at a second-term aggregate low of 38.1% (Silver Bulletin, net -19.1) and a +8 generic congressional ballot lead for Democrats. FBI arrested senior CIA official David Rush after finding 400+ gold bars ($40M+) and $2M cash at his Virginia home. The ceasefire technically holds through Day 89 but diplomats warn any miscalculation could restart hostilities.
